text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Labour minister defends Industrial Court against charges its recent awards to pilots and bankers were exorbitant.
- Norway criticises the conduct of the trial of Koigi wa Wamwere who with two others were convicted and jailed for four years.
- A 30-man gang terrorises priests and nuns at a Roman Catholic diocesan residence.
- Kenyan secondary school teachers to sit-in over pay.
- Nairobi mayor ordered to keep out of city, town halls by government when not on official duties.
- Bomb scare at chambers of Attorney-General Amos Wako.
- Major changes on electoral boundaries and the shifting of divisions to other regions displace several parliamentarians.
- Two car-jackers who violently robbed a Tanzanian tourist are sentenced to hang.
- Association of Local Government Authorities disassociates itself from Nairobi mayor's call for more mayoral powers. ($1=56 Kenyan shillings)
